dmm-2006-tiebreaker-01.title: Parametrize
dmm-2006-tiebreaker-01.body:
$a^2=c^2-b^2=(c-b)(c+b)=289(2b+289)$ (as $c+b=2b+289$). Since $289=17^2$, $17\mid a$; write $a=17m$, so $m^2=2b+289$ (and $m$ is odd). Then $b=\frac{m^2-289}2$, $c=b+289=\frac{m^2+289}2$. Not all even holds automatically since $a=17m$ is odd.

$a<b$ means $17m<\frac{m^2-289}2$, i.e. $m^2-34m-289>0$, i.e. $m>17+17\sqrt2\approx41.04$. The smallest odd such $m$ is $43$, giving $a=731$, $b=780$, $c=1069$.

**Answer: 1069**

dmm-2006-tiebreaker-02.title: Write $b^2$ in base $a$
dmm-2006-tiebreaker-02.body:
$a^2=(11)_b=b+1$, so $b=a^2-1$ and $b^2=(a^2-1)^2=a^4-2a^2+1$. Now
$$a^4-2a^2+1=(a-1)a^3+(a-2)a^2+0\cdot a+1\quad(a\ge3),$$
(check: $(a-1)a^3+(a-2)a^2+1=a^4-a^3+a^3-2a^2+1$). So in base $a$, $b^2$ has digits $(a-1),(a-2),0,1$ and the third digit from the right is $a-2$. For $a=2$ ($b=3$, $b^2=9=1001_2$) the third digit is $0=a-2$ as well.

**Answer: $a-2$**

dmm-2006-tiebreaker-03.title: Use the roots
dmm-2006-tiebreaker-03.body:
The roots $\varphi,\psi$ of $x^2-x-1$ satisfy $x^n=F_nx+F_{n-1}$ (Fibonacci numbers), so $x^{10}=55x+34$ and $x^9=34x+21$. Then $ax^{10}+bx^9+1=(55a+34b)x+(34a+21b+1)$ at $x=\varphi,\psi$. Both vanish if $55a+34b=0$ and $34a+21b=-1$. Solving: $a=-\frac{34}{55}b$, so $b\left(21-\frac{34^2}{55}\right)=-1$, i.e. $b\cdot\frac{1155-1156}{55}=-1$, $b=55$, $a=-34$.

These are the only values: the two conditions at $\varphi$ and $\psi$ form a linear system with unique solution (the determinant $\varphi^{10}\psi^9-\psi^{10}\varphi^9=(\varphi\psi)^9(\varphi-\psi)\ne0$).

**Answer: $a=-34,\ b=55$** (indeed $-34x^{10}+55x^9+1=(x^2-x-1)(\ldots)$).
